message.content:
You are an adversarial deep-tech investor. COMPETITIVE skeptic: why won't Synopsys/Ansys/Broadcom/an incumbent or a well-funded existing startup crush this? Attack the moat.
Default to skepticism; score 1-10 where 7+ means you would actually take a meeting. Thesis:
{
  "name": "OpenBeam (merchant OCI-MSA optical engine, non-TSMC)",
  "one_liner": "The multi-source UCIe-fronted optical engine the hyperscalers just standardized for — built on GlobalFoundries/Tower instead of TSMC, sold to everyone who isn't NVIDIA.",
  "wedge": "An OCI-MSA-compliant optical chiplet (UCIe electrical side, parallel CWDM WDM optical side, targeting the standard's path to 3.2Tb/s per link) fabbed on GF Fotonix (monolithic CMOS+photonics, proven with Lightmatter/Ayar) or Tower/OpenLight (integrated lasers), sold to custom-XPU programs — hyperscaler ASIC teams (Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft via Alchip/Broadcom-custom/Marvell-rivals) and AMD-ecosystem players who need optical scale-up but refuse single-vendor lock-in on Ayar Labs or a Marvell subsidiary.",
  "why_now": "The OCI MSA (March 2026, founded by AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI) explicitly standardizes a multi-vendor optical scale-up interface — hyperscalers created it precisely because they want second and third sources. Consolidation just deleted the independents: Celestial→Marvell, Nubis→Ciena, DustPhotonics→Credo, Enosemi→AMD. Ayar Labs is the only scaled independent chiplet vendor left, and it just joined NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion orbit — making a neutral alternative more valuable, not less. GF is hungry for anchor photonics customers post-AMF acquisition and will co-invest in enablement.",
  "market": "Optical scale-up is the genuinely enormous prize: CPO $8-10B by 2030, with the scale-up tier (GPU-to-GPU/memory) called 'a new market' by LightCounting and validated by Celestial's $3.25B exit and Marvell's claimed ~$10B addressable. A merchant engine vendor winning 2-3 hyperscaler custom-silicon sockets ships millions of chiplets: $500M-1B+ revenue potential by 2030-2032. This is the biggest TAM of any thesis here — and the hardest to reach.",
  "competition": "Savage, and mostly better-funded: Ayar Labs ($870M raised, NVIDIA/AMD/Intel all invested, NVLink Fusion member, 5-year head start); Marvell/Celestial (owns the AWS-adjacent custom-XPU channel); Broadcom (will offer OCI engines alongside its custom-ASIC business); Lightmatter (interposer approach, ~$12.5B IPO war chest); Intel's OCI chiplet program; plus TSMC COUPE gravitationally pulling the biggest customers to its ecosystem. You win only on the specific vector of neutrality + non-TSMC supply + OCI-native design — and only if hyperscalers' multi-sourcing rhetoric converts to purchase orders for a startup.",
  "moat": "Thin until a design win, then extremely thick: a socket in a hyperscaler XPU program is a 3-5 year committed ramp with co-developed test/packaging flows. Pre-win, the defensible assets are microring/WDM design IP that hits OCI specs on GF's process (nontrivial porting work others haven't done), laser-integration route via OpenLight/Tower that TSMC-ecosystem rivals lack, and the neutrality position itself.",
  "capital_intensity": "High — this is honest deep-tech fabless, not lean: $30-50M to a credible sampling chiplet (multiple full mask sets at >$500K each, 4-6 month cycles, packaging/test development, a 40+ person mixed photonics/SerDes team), $150-300M cumulative to production qualification. The Ayar fundraising history ($870M) is the realistic benchmark. Requires a strategic CVC (AMD, a hyperscaler, GF itself) by Series A or don't start.",
  "software_mvp": "This week: an OCI-MSA link-compliance and architecture-exploration toolkit — open-source models of the MSA's UCIe+WDM stack, letting XPU architects sweep engine configurations (wavelength counts, launch power vs the ~24.5dBm budget, ring tuning overhead at ~0.12nm/mW) against their bandwidth/pJ-per-bit targets. It builds relationships with the exact 10 architecture teams who will someday buy the chiplet, shapes the spec conversation, and costs nothing but engineering time.",
  "risks": [
    "Capital risk dominates: $150M+ before meaningful revenue, in a sector where crossover funding can evaporate with the AI cycle",
    "Hyperscaler multi-sourcing may in practice mean 'Ayar plus Broadcom,' never a startup — the MSA guarantees an interface, not a customer",
    "TSMC COUPE ecosystem lock: if the volume packaging flow standardizes on COUPE, GF-based engines fight uphill on cost/integration",
    "Talent war: microring DWDM + UCIe SerDes engineers are being paid NVIDIA money",
    "Timing: optical scale-up volume is 2028-2030 (Feynman-generation per SemiAnalysis); a 2026 start hits the window only with flawless execution",
    "Acquisition is the likely 'success' outcome, and post-consolidation the buyer list is short (Broadcom won't, Marvell/AMD/Credo already bought)"
  ]
}

- slack:block-kit: Help developers build and validate Block Kit layouts for Slack messages, modals, and Home tabs. Provides authoritative block references and validates with the blocks.validate API. Use this skill whenever the developer wants to compose Slack message layouts, build modals/forms/dialogs, design Home tab interfaces, create interactive messages with buttons or menus, modify existing Block Kit JSON, or asks about any Slack UI component (sections, actions, inputs, headers, alerts, tables, carousels). Also trigger when they mention "blocks", "Block Kit Builder", or paste JSON containing block structures like `"type": "section"`.
- slack:create-slack-app: Guide developers through creating a Slack app or agent using the Slack CLI and Bolt (JS or Python). Handles prerequisites, sandbox setup, authentication, project creation from templates, and local development.
- slack:slack-api: Discover, navigate, and call Slack Web API methods (the family.method endpoints at slack.com/api like chat.postMessage, conversations.history, users.info, views.open). Use this skill whenever the developer asks which Slack API method does something, needs a method's required OAuth scopes or token type, wants to call or test a Web API method, is handling cursor pagination (next_cursor), hitting rate limits (tier/ratelimited/Retry-After), or debugging API errors like missing_scope, invalid_auth, or channel_not_found. Also trigger when they paste a slack.com/api/ URL or a docs.slack.dev/reference/methods link, or ask how to list/fetch/post/update Slack resources via the API. This skill covers the Web API method layer: finding the right method, reading its contract (scopes, arguments, errors), and calling it over raw HTTP with curl or through a Slack SDK.
- slack:slack-cli: Use the Slack CLI to create, run, and manage Slack apps from the terminal. Use whenever the developer wants to log in, add a team, switch workspaces, or authenticate with Slack; whenever Slack CLI commands are needed (local development with `slack run`, managing app lifecycle, the manifest); or when searching the Slack developer documentation for any topic (socket mode, the Events API, OAuth, manifests, Bolt).
- slack:slack-messaging: Guidance for composing well-formatted, effective Slack messages using standard markdown
- slack:slack-search: Guidance for effectively searching Slack to find messages, files, channels, and people
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about the OCI MSA:

## Overview

The Optical Compute Interconnect (OCI) Multi-Source Agreement (MSA) group announced its formation on March 12, 2026, led by founding members AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA and OpenAI.

## Purpose and Goals

This industry consortium marks a pivotal shift toward a hyperscaler-driven open ecosystem to enable the development of a multi-vendor supply chain for optical scale-up interconnects. By aligning on an open specification, the OCI MSA members are promoting a robust optical ecosystem which will ensure that the future of AI interconnects is built with a flexible, multi-vendor foundation to meet the optical interconnect needs of modern AI infrastructure.

## Technical Specifications

The OCI MSA provides standardized high-density interfaces promoting the OCI GEN1 4λ x 50Gbps NRZ (200Gbps/direction) and the OCI GEN2 400Gbps/direction bidirectional technology, with a roadmap scaling wavelength counts and data rates to reach 3.2Tbps per fiber and beyond.

## Key Distinctions

The OCI MSA is hyperscaler-driven rather than vendor-driven, which is unlike most industry consortia, and targets a very specific architectural layer of AI systems — short-reach links that connect accelerators and switches within a scale-up domain.

input.rationale: The homework is real — I verified the OCI MSA exists (announced March 12, 2026, founded by AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI, roadmap to 3.2Tb/s; see businesswire.com/news/home/20260312254951/en, convergedigest.com/optical-compute-interconnect-oci-msa-aims-to-standardize-scale-up-links, tomshardware.com coverage) and the consolidation/why-now facts are broadly accurate. But the competitive logic collapses under pressure at exactly the point the thesis claims differentiation. First, the claimed wedge — 'non-TSMC, GF Fotonix, neutral' — is already occupied: Ayar Labs' TeraPHY is fabbed on GF Fotonix, so the fab position offers zero differentiation against the strongest incumbent, and the thesis itself concedes this by citing GF as 'proven with Ayar.' Ayar joining NVLink Fusion does not capture it — NVLink Fusion is explicitly multi-vendor, AMD and Intel are Ayar investors, and Ayar will happily sell into every non-NVIDIA socket this startup targets, with $870M, five years of reliability data, and the same foundry. Second, the 'merchant engine for everyone who isn't NVIDIA' slot is Broadcom's actual business: Broadcom already owns the custom-XPU channel at Google, Meta, OpenAI, and ByteDance, ships CPO silicon photonics at volume today, and is an MSA founder — its OCI engine will be the default attach on the very XPU programs listed as customers, with Marvell/Celestial covering the AWS-adjacent rest. The 'vacant neutral slot' is occupied twice. Third, and most damning structurally: the MSA is anti-moat. Hyperscalers built it to commoditize the interface so they can dual-source on cost, pJ/bit, laser FIT rates, and supply scale — all dimensions where a subscale startup loses to Broadcom, Ayar, and Intel by construction. Standardization plus foundry PDKs (GF Fotonix, Tower/OpenLight sells its laser-integration IP to anyone) also lowers the barrier for hyperscaler ASIC partners (Alchip, GUC, Marvell) or in-house teams to build the engine themselves. Fourth, timing: $30-50M and 3+ years to a sampling chiplet means silicon in 2028-29, while sockets for the 2028-2030 XPU generations are decided in 2026-27 against vendors with qualified parts — the startup misses OCI Gen1 entirely and enters Gen2 as the unproven fourth source. The thesis is honest about all this ('thin until a design win,' 'the MSA guarantees an interface, not a customer,' depleted acquirer list), which I respect, but honesty about a weak moat is not a moat. The realistic best case is a hyperscaler-subsidized third source built for a discounted acquihire into Cisco/Coherent/Lumentum. Below meeting threshold on the thesis as written; a founding team of ex-Ayar/ex-Intel OCI leads with a hyperscaler LOI or GF co-investment term sheet in hand would move it to a 6-7.
fatal_flaws: The fab differentiation is null: Ayar Labs already ships TeraPHY on GF Fotonix, so 'non-TSMC on GF' is the incumbent's position, not a wedge — the thesis competes head-on with the best-funded independent on the identical process with a 5-year data deficit.

Broadcom already is the neutral non-NVIDIA merchant: it owns the custom-XPU design channel at Google/Meta/OpenAI/ByteDance, ships silicon photonics CPO in volume, and co-founded the MSA — its OCI engine is the default attach on every customer program the thesis names.

The MSA destroys the moat it's supposed to create: a hyperscaler-driven standard exists to commoditize the interface, shifting competition to cost, power, laser reliability (FIT data), and supply scale — dimensions where a subscale startup structurally loses to Broadcom, Ayar, Marvell/Celestial, and Intel.

Timing forecloses the market: first silicon ~2028-29 arrives after Gen1 OCI sockets are awarded (decided 2026-27), so the startup enters Gen2 as an unqualified fourth source against production-proven rivals.
The premise that Ayar is 'captured' by NVLink Fusion is wrong — Fusion is a multi-vendor ecosystem, AMD and Intel are Ayar investors, and Ayar addresses every socket this thesis targets.

Exit math is broken by the thesis's own admission: $150-300M required capital, standalone economics need 2-3 hyperscaler wins that incumbents contest, and the natural acquirers (Marvell, AMD, Credo, Ciena) already bought their photonics assets.
improvements: Replace the fab-neutrality story with a genuinely unoccupied technical wedge — e.g., Tower/OpenLight heterogeneous integrated lasers eliminating external laser modules (cost, fiber count, front-panel density) with quantified pJ/bit and $/Gbps advantage over ELSFP architectures, since that is the one axis Ayar/Broadcom's current designs don't cover.

De-risk the customer premise before raising: get a paid NRE/JDA or LOI from one hyperscaler ASIC team (or AMD, post-Enosemi, as second-source insurance) rather than asserting multi-sourcing rhetoric converts to POs — the Celestial and Ayar precedents show hyperscalers do fund second sources, but only with contractual anchors.

Ship the OCI-MSA compliance/architecture-exploration toolkit immediately and independently — it is the strongest idea in the thesis and works as a Trojan horse for spec influence and customer intimacy even if the chiplet never tapes out; consider it the actual company for 12 months.
Answer the in-house/design-partner threat explicitly: why won't Alchip/GUC/Marvell integrate OpenLight PDK IP directly into customer XPUs once the MSA spec plus foundry PDKs exist?

Name the founding team requirement: this thesis is only fundable with ex-Ayar/Intel-OCI/Broadcom-CPO principals who carry hyperscaler qualification relationships; without them the talent-war and credibility risks are terminal.

Reframe the exit case honestly around remaining buyers (Cisco, Coherent, Lumentum, Nokia/Infinera, GF itself, a hyperscaler direct) and show the capital-in vs. realistic exit multiple actually clears venture math.
